review.description: S1/S3 now populate saved projections and recover a shared cursor, and S7 adds direct sidebar launch with a controlled 50 ms every-sample gate. Actual ChatGPT and typed-chat timings remain separate. Older history remains inspectable until explicit continuation; restoring an earlier database requires every view and incremental history cursor to resync.
review.implementation: Inspected atomic WAL publication and cursor history, authenticated app-only reads/watch, independent-process reconciliation and deferred embedded startup. Transcript reads follow run invalidations and preserve local output/drafts. Subscription versions now use a local monotonic revision; Agent separately tracks full resync and explicit history browsing mode. The initial projection ignores lifetime invalidations, output-only publications reuse unrelated summaries, and repository invalidations reload dependent saved freshness. Saved transcript reads now use one stable coalescing pump, preserving progress during continued streaming and pausing further pages on hide. Current-view transport errors retain dedicated feedback and retry without a new event. Hidden older reads cannot consume later dirty domains.
review.tests: The production test retains 20 fresh and 10 warm measurements with delayed provider operations. Commit, burst, reconnect, resync, hidden-view and query-response tests assert saved-state ordering; existing transcript/recovery fixtures remain required. The strengthened launch assertion requires both GitHub synchronization and AI assessment still pending at shell usability. TestProductionShellPrecedesDeferredRuntime guards the actual production resource order after hosted samples exposed head-payload parsing cost. Three restored-database browser scenarios cover reports, plugins, saved detail and transcript drafts, and a 1,300-event window remains stable under published updates. Startup journal, output-domain, transcript-only subscription and repository-only resume regressions cover those boundaries; BenchmarkUIOutputPublication profiles the retained 1,000/3,000/100 workload. Continuing slow-read streaming and no-new-publication visibility regressions verify that progress and resumption do not depend on EOF. Hidden full resync advances the read generation before visibility-based refresh, so delayed higher-cursor replies cannot poison restored state. Targeted regressions prove normal hidden catch-up for Messages, query recovery with idle healthy watches and observation-only review completion. Direct fixture-host HTTP delivery replaces page.route mocking; the same launch handler and production resource remain timed with no fresh-context prefetch. The launch gate now proves actual visible text paints for all six nav entries with FCP corroboration and unchanged strict50ms; callbacks and notification delivery remain independently auditable.
